## What was delivered

`tests/org/apache/commons/csv/LexerAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 3.8 test (`extends junit.framework.TestCase`, no external helpers), in package `org.apache.commons.csv` so it can reach the package-private abstract `Lexer`.

### Approach
- `Lexer` is abstract + package-private, constructed from a `CSVFormat` and a package-private `ExtendedBufferedReader`. The file defines a tiny private `ConcreteLexer extends Lexer` stub (only to satisfy the abstract `nextToken(Token)`, never invoked) and builds readers from `new ExtendedBufferedReader(new StringReader(...))`.
- `api/` only documents `Lexer`, so custom formats are built via this project's builder API (`CSVFormat.newBuilder(CSVFormat.DEFAULT).withDelimiter(...)/.withEscape(...)/.withCommentStart(...)/.withIgnoreEmptyLines(...)/.withIgnoreSurroundingSpaces(...).build()`) — the fluent `CSVFormat.withX` / `newFormat` methods don't exist in this (pre‑1.0) version, confirmed by trial compilation.

### Coverage (33 tests), all tied to the Javadoc contract
- **constructor/fields**: `format` and `in` are kept by reference; `ignoreEmptyLines` / `ignoreSurroundingSpaces` mirror the supplied format (tested both true and false).
- **getLineNumber()**: 0 before any read; advances to 2 after draining `"a\nb\nc"`.
- **isDelimiter / isQuoteChar / isEscape / isCommentStart**: default `,` / `"` / none / none, plus configured-value cases; negative cases for non-matching chars.
- **isWhitespace**: true for space/tab, false for letters, digits, `"` and the delimiter.
- **isStartOfLine**: true for CR/LF, false for content chars.
- **isEndOfFile**: true for `-1`, false for `'a'`, `0`, space, `'\n'`.
- **readEndOfLine**: bare `\n`, bare `\r` (following char left in stream), greedy `\r\n` (second char silently consumed — verified via next `read()`), and rejection of ordinary chars / `-1`.
- **readEscape**: `\n`→LF, `\t`→TAB, `\r`→CR; throws `IOException` when the escape char is last in the stream (documented); returns the end‑of‑stream marker for an invalid escape (`\q`), verified through `isEndOfFile(...)` and `getLastChar()`.
- **trimTrailingSpaces**: trailing spaces removed, clean text untouched, all-spaces→empty, empty buffer no-op, leading/interior spaces preserved — all asserting the resulting buffer contents.
